**Dynasty:** 宋

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The twelve-*juǎn* magnum opus of the senior Southern-Sòng lay-Buddhist scholar [王日休](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%97%A5%E4%BC%91) Wáng Rìxiū (d. 1173), styled *Lóngshū jūshì* 龍舒居士. The full title — "Expanded" (*zēngguǎng*) — reflects an expanded recension of an earlier shorter version of the text; the work circulated in multiple recensions in the late twelfth and thirteenth centuries before stabilising in the standard twelve-*juǎn* form preserved in the canon. The *Jìngtǔ wén* is the most widely circulated and influential lay-Buddhist Pure Land treatise of pre-Yuán China, and remained one of the principal Pure Land popularising works through the late-imperial period.

**Abstract**

Wáng Rìxiū writes as a Confucian-trained scholar (he held the *jìnshì* degree) who has resigned from official service to dedicate himself to Pure Land cultivation. The *Jìngtǔ wén* is structured for the lay reader — without specialist Buddhist doctrinal jargon, with extensive narrative and practical-devotional material, and with a clear organising structure that walks the reader through (a) the doctrinal rationale for Pure Land devotion, (b) practical instructions for daily *niànfó*, (c) hagiographies of Pure Land practitioners, (d) responses to common doubts and objections, (e) verse and devotional material for daily recitation. The combination of doctrinal-popularising prose, abundant biographical material, and direct lay-practical guidance is the formula that made the work so successful.

The *Jìngtǔ wén* draws extensively on the canonical Pure Land sūtras, on [道綽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E7%B6%BD) Dàochuò's *Ānlè jí* [KR6p0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0037), on [懷感](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E6%84%9F) Huáigǎn's *Qúnyí lùn* [KR6p0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0039), and on the post-Sòng Tiāntái-Pure Land synthesis associated with [知禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E7%A6%AE) Sìmíng Zhīlǐ and [遵式](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%B5%E5%BC%8F) Cíyún Zūnshì. Wáng Rìxiū is also distinctively engaged with classical Confucian literature — he draws explicit analogies between Buddhist and Confucian moral teaching, and his Pure Land recommendations are presented in a register accessible to literati readers.

The work also contains the famous synthetic recension of the *Larger Sukhāvatīvyūma* — the *Dà ēmítuó jīng* 大阿彌陀經 [KR6f0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0064) — that Wáng Rìxiū compiled by collating four of the five extant Chinese translations of the larger sūtra into a single coherent text. This recension is the principal precedent for [魏源](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E6%BA%90) Wèi Yuán's *Huìyì* [KR6p0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0001) of the late Qīng. The *Jìngtǔ wén* preserves Wáng Rìxiū's editorial discussion of the recension; the recension itself circulates separately as [KR6f0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0064).

The Taishō text is collated against the Korean canon, *original* (原), and the *Yuan* canon. Dating: c. 1160–1173 covers Wáng Rìxiū's mature period and the period of his death.
